nodes.title: Keep the page index in a signal
nodes.why: The 0-based index is the only value that changes. Holding it in a signal lets every computed value and the OnPush template update when Previous or Next changes it.
nodes.alternative: Keep currentPage as a plain number and recompute the slice in getters.
nodes.tradeoff: Getters work while every change starts with a click in this template, but they rerun on every check and miss changes made later from a timer or a service under OnPush; the signal adds call syntax in the template.

nodes.title: Derive total pages from data size
nodes.why: The page count follows the collection size and still gives one page for an empty dataset, so the label and the last-page check stay valid.
nodes.alternative: Hard-code the number of pages independently from the rows.
nodes.tradeoff: A minimum of one keeps the controls simple, though some products prefer an explicit zero-page empty state.

nodes.title: Derive only the visible rows
nodes.why: slice copies one page without touching USERS, and the computed keeps that page until currentPage changes.
nodes.alternative: Splice the canonical users array as navigation changes, or slice inline in the template.
nodes.tradeoff: The computed holds one small array per page, but navigation stays reversible and the template binds a single value.

nodes.title: Stop navigation at the last page
nodes.why: The guard keeps currentPage inside the page range even if goToNext() is called while the Next button is disabled.
nodes.alternative: Rely only on a disabled Next button in the template.
nodes.tradeoff: The boundary is checked in two places, but the method stays correct for programmatic callers.
